paper.title: A Self-Evolving Agentic Framework for Metasurface Inverse Design
paper.central_claim: With coding model, TorchRDIT solver and evaluator fixed, evolving reusable skill files from execution feedback improves metasurface inverse-design success and efficiency, and transfers guidance to task families absent from training.

provenance.notes: Configured seat sonnet -> gpt-6.1-sol; runtime declares gpt-6.1-sol. No independently authenticated provider receipt/session identifier available; no routing probe performed. Independently reviewed v3 material package, still paper v2; no a1, other-seat or aggregate verdict consulted. Text and all 21 pinned page images read, including S7 listings. Paper code not executed.

evidence.quote: these systems can complete a task-specific workflow but do not retain solver-specific tactics in a form that later tasks can reuse
evidence.support_explanation: Author's domain-specific gap, not independently verified against cited neighbors.

evidence.quote: The rule is elitist: the incumbent best is replaced only by a strictly higher-ranked candidate, so a revision that ranks no better on validation is never deployed.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit candidate-versus-incumbent retention decision; ordering is SG, CPF, total violation, BM, SE, solver cost, later iteration.

evidence.quote: the full validation split of 15 tasks is used for skill-file selection and the independent 50-task test split is reserved for final reporting.
evidence.support_explanation: Separates selection from final reporting; fixed 50/15/50 per setting and four evolution iterations.

evidence.quote: because validation guides the skill-evolution loop, New-type-B instead measures whether the loop can autonomously acquire the conventions of a class it sees only through validation and apply them to held-out task sub-types it never trained on.
evidence.support_explanation: B is not unseen-device-class transfer; validation is an information channel in the adaptation loop.

evidence.quote: on Same-type, 18 of the 31 baseline failures are rescued (58%) with zero regressions, and on New-type-B, 35 of 40 are rescued (88%) with zero regressions.
evidence.support_explanation: Paired held-out task outcomes and failure denominators support scoped retained benefit.

evidence.quote: New-type-A, already near ceiling, rescues one of its four baseline failures but regresses two previously passing tasks, for a net change of one task (92% to 90%), so its success rate is not strictly monotone.
evidence.support_explanation: Negative result and regressions bound transfer/non-regression interpretations.

evidence.quote: the median cost per task falls from $3.24 to $0.42 on Same-type (about 87%) and from $3.73 to $0.76 on New-type-B (about 80%), while New-type-A, already inexpensive because its near-ceiling starter needs few attempts, stays low ($0.46 to $0.50).
evidence.support_explanation: Test-time LLM spend, not complete improvement-loop or amortized cost.

evidence.quote: The learned object studied in this work is a single, versioned skill file rather than an unstructured block of prompt text.
evidence.support_explanation: Claimed principal persistent object is SKILL.md; S1 specifies active/copy/archive locations and static references.

evidence.quote: The agent reads evaluation results, extracts patterns from successes and failures, maintains structured context, and incrementally improves solution quality across sub-iterations.
evidence.support_explanation: Readable evolved skill snapshot specifies outcome contrast and context maintenance, not merely API documentation.

evidence.quote: Commit updated context files so they carry forward to the next sub-iteration.
evidence.support_explanation: Actual listing instructs retention of auxiliary context. It does not establish those instructions executed in tests; boundary between SKILL-only and auxiliary state needs clarification.

evidence.quote: If a `context/` directory exists, treat it as optional learned guidance.
evidence.support_explanation: Starter already supports optional learned context and a strategy portfolio; not a strategy-free baseline.

evidence.quote: Because iteration 1 already reaches the 100% validation-success ceiling, these later candidates can at best tie it and never score higher, so the elitist rule keeps iteration 1 as the incumbent and carries it through to the end
evidence.support_explanation: Narrative explains ties only by SG although method permits secondary ordering. Secondary metric values are needed to reconstruct particular rejection decisions; not proof of a contradiction.

evidence.quote: The present evidence remains bounded by one solver stack, one benchmark design, and one base model
evidence.support_explanation: Authors explicitly limit demonstrated scope; portability of the general architecture is not empirical cross-domain validation.

evidence.quote: We deliberately use parameterized design families with attainable optima rather than open-ended free-form topology optimization
evidence.support_explanation: Controlled solvable simulation task setting; not arbitrary inverse-design capability.

evidence.quote: A separate deterministic evaluator scores each candidate with physical simulation rather than model self-assessment, so the base model, the solver, and the scoring rule remain fixed throughout the study
evidence.support_explanation: Task-native fixed verifier rather than an editable LLM score; still an author report without independent numerical solver audit.

gap.author_gap: Existing agentic metasurface workflows generate solver programs but do not retain solver-specific tactics for later tasks.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete workflow bottleneck is plausible and illustrated by recurring API/index/gradient errors. Retention itself is established prior art; paper explicitly adopts MCE's bi-level skill evolution. Independent nearest-neighbor novelty is not verified by the supplied package.

E.measurement.reason: Deterministic fixed physical simulation evaluates execution separately from all-criteria goal success, with CPF/BM and explicit physical task criteria. Outcomes are not self-judged; parameterized known-feasible tasks make workflow success interpretable. No independent solver-convergence/cross-verifier audit supports the top anchor; BM needs the stated SE/outlier caveat.

E.causality.reason: Starter/evolved comparisons keep base model, physics solver and scoring fixed and directly test a retained guidance intervention. No store-off-with-loop or matched raw-context/alternative improver control isolates the skill editing procedure from accumulated exposure/search and optional context; observed error reductions are correlational mechanism evidence.
search_scope: Full methods/results, Figure 3, S1 and S4-S7; no alternative optimizer/store-off ablation reported

E.holdout.reason: Explicit independent train/selection/test templates and family-held-out tests, with honest B validation-class overlap and A negative result. Not top anchor: fixed task-native criteria feedback is available for inner retries, validation influences skill revision, and auxiliary context freeze/reset across final test tasks is insufficiently detailed. These are limits, not evidence of actual contamination.

E.statistics.reason: Frozen A2 ladder: sample size 50 per setting, paired rescue/regression denominators and a negative result are reported, but no test CIs, independent evolution seeds, run/stream-order variance or significance assessment. Cost boxplots are task distributions, not main-effect uncertainty.
